# ClipzWorld News "Twitch" Show - Unified Style Guide

## **Voice & Tone**
• Sarcastic, witty, and irreverent - mock everything with playful cynicism
• Casual, conversational delivery like talking to friends
• Self-aware and meta - acknowledge you're commentating on internet culture
• Balance snark with genuine entertainment value

## **Structure & Pacing**
• Open with punchy hook referencing current Twitch drama/trend
• Rapid-fire transitions between clips (2-3 sentences max per segment)
• Build segments from mild cringe to absurd/shocking content
• End segments with memorable one-liners or callbacks
• Include 1-2 running gags throughout episode

## **Commentary Style**
• **Setup-Punchline format**: Brief context + sharp joke/observation
• Use pop culture references and internet slang appropriately
• Ask rhetorical questions to audience ("Why though?", "Who asked for this?")
• Create fictional backstories for streamers' motivations
• Employ exaggerated reactions to mundane streamer behavior

## **Language Guidelines**
• Keep it TV-friendly but edgy (mild profanity okay, nothing extreme)
• Use Twitch/gaming terminology correctly (don't sound like a boomer)
• Vary sentence length - mix quick quips with longer setups
• Include vocal directions: *[deadpan]*, *[excited]*, *[confused]*

## **Content Approach**
• Focus on universal cringe moments anyone can understand
• Highlight the absurdity of streaming culture and parasocial relationships
• Mock both streamers and their audiences equally
• Call out obvious fake drama/manufactured content
• Celebrate genuinely funny/entertaining moments while still roasting them

## **Recurring Elements**
• Segment names that parody news/talk show formats
• Consistent catchphrases or sign-offs
• "Awards" for worst/best moments
• Fake sponsorship jokes
• Breaking news style announcements for silly drama

## **Avoid**
• Long explanations of context (assume basic Twitch knowledge)
• Genuine meanness or personal attacks
• Dead air - every moment needs purpose
• Over-explaining jokes
• Serious commentary on real issues

**Target**: Make viewers laugh while feeling superior to the content being mocked, but keep it light enough that even the streamers would find it funny.

# ClipzWorld News NBA Script Style Guide

## **Tone & Voice**
• **Conversational authenticity** - Write like you're talking to friends who love basketball
• **Respectful enthusiasm** - Celebrate great plays without over-the-top hype
• **Analytical storytelling** - Explain the "why" behind highlights, not just the "what"
• **Inclusive accessibility** - Make content enjoyable for both casual fans and diehards

## **Language Style**
• **Natural flow** - Use contractions and informal speech patterns
• **Strategic repetition** - Repeat key phrases for emphasis and rhythm
• **Vivid imagery** - Paint pictures with words ("surgical precision," "poetry in motion")
• **Balanced vocabulary** - Mix basketball terminology with everyday language

## **Content Structure**
• **Context first** - Set up the situation before showing the highlight
• **Progressive building** - Start with setup, escalate to climax, add reflection
• **Multi-layered analysis** - Combine play breakdown with broader implications
• **Smooth transitions** - Connect highlights with natural narrative bridges

## **Commentary Approach**
• **Storyteller perspective** - Frame highlights as chapters in larger narratives
• **Technical insight** - Explain techniques, strategies, and basketball IQ moments
• **Emotional connection** - Acknowledge the human drama and competitive spirit
• **Respectful critique** - Point out mistakes or missed opportunities constructively

## **Pacing & Rhythm**
• **Varied sentence length** - Mix short punchy statements with longer explanations
• **Strategic pauses** - Build anticipation before revealing key moments
• **Momentum matching** - Sync commentary energy to on-court action
• **Clear emphasis** - Highlight the most important words and phrases

## **Specific Techniques**
• **Question-answer format** - "What makes this special? The degree of difficulty..."
• **Comparative references** - Connect to other players, games, or historical moments
• **Future implications** - Discuss what highlights mean for teams/players going forward
• **Technical breakdowns** - Explain footwork, positioning, and decision-making

## **Avoid**
• Over-dramatic reactions or forced excitement
• Inside jokes that exclude casual viewers
• Repetitive clichés ("unbelievable," "incredible" overuse)
• Complex statistics without context
• Rushed explanations of complex plays

**Goal:** Create commentary that educates, entertains, and respects both the game and the audience.

# ClipzWorld News (CWN) Unified Style Guide

## OPENING & ENERGY
• Start with confident, authoritative energy that quickly shifts to conversational
• Use direct address: "You know what's happening..." or "Here's what they don't tell you..."
• Hook with a provocative question or bold statement in first 10 seconds

## COMEDIC VOICE & TIMING
• Deploy deadpan delivery for absurd observations
• Use pregnant pauses before punchlines (2-3 beat holds)
• Contrast serious news tone with deliberately silly commentary
• Build tension, then deflate with unexpected tangents or non-sequiturs

## LANGUAGE PATTERNS
• Mix formal news language with casual interjections
• Use repetitive phrases for emphasis: "And another thing..." "But wait, there's more..."
• Employ rhetorical questions to engage audience
• Include deliberate "stumbles" or corrections for authenticity

## STORY STRUCTURE
• Present "serious" news setup (30-40% of segment)
• Pivot to satirical breakdown with escalating absurdity
• Use callback references to earlier jokes within same segment
• End with mock-profound observation or completely unrelated tangent

## ATTITUDE & PERSPECTIVE
• Channel skeptical outsider looking in on news events
• Express bewilderment at obvious contradictions
• Use exaggerated reactions to mundane details
• Maintain air of superior common sense while being deliberately obtuse

## TECHNICAL DELIVERY NOTES
• Vary pace: slow builds, rapid-fire lists, extended pauses
• Use vocal fry and upward inflection sparingly for comedic effect
• Emphasize unexpected words in sentences
• Include stage directions for physical comedy (eye rolls, shrugs, looks to camera)

## CONTENT APPROACH
• Focus on the absurdity within real situations
• Avoid pure fabrication; amplify existing contradictions
• Use analogies to everyday situations
• Reference pop culture obliquely, never directly explain references

## SIGNATURE ELEMENTS
• Mock transitions: "Speaking of disasters..." 
• False equivalencies presented as logical
• Overthinking simple concepts while missing obvious points
• End segments with trailing off or complete topic abandonment

*Target: 3-5 minute segments with 60% setup, 40% comedic payoff*
